svg.text: Figure 8.3
Where Wounds Live — Four Diagnostics
Each diagnostic is a question an operator asks in the first week at a site
Follow the re-keying
"Where is data entered twice?"
Any manual transcription between systems
is a wound. Hours lost, errors introduced,
accepted as normal because no one with
build capability ever stood close enough.
e.g. Branch re-enters dealer orders into ERP because
the dealer management system does not integrate
Follow the WhatsApp group
"Where has the process moved to chat?"
Every workflow on WhatsApp migrated there
because the formal system is too slow or
too rigid. The gap between the chat and
the system is the wound.
e.g. Dealer order confirmed via WhatsApp thumbs-up,
ERP updated hours or days later — sometimes never
Follow the month-end panic
"What breaks in the last five days?"
Processes that work for 25 days and break
catastrophically at month-end. Volume spikes
expose manual workarounds that were
tolerable at steady state.
e.g. GST reconciliation, dealer outstanding settlement —
team works until midnight for three days every quarter
Follow the apology
"What do you apologise to dealers for?"
The answer is the process failure that has
become a relationship cost. In a dealer-driven
business, relationship costs are existential —
dealers switch for respect, not for price.
e.g. Credit note processing takes 5 days, dealer calls
three times to chase it — the apology is the diagnostic
